delivery_checks: An ad-hoc idea from Krish is built, shown to him, and queued only after he approves the exact payload.

Made in a Claude session, with the Codex plugin building it (Ruling, Krish, 2026-11-13; content-engine docs/CAROUSEL-STANDARD.md, "How a carousel is made"): the session writes the words and the direction, a Codex card of kind meme builds the picture in code, and the session verifies it against the brand palette before Krish sees it; never a scheduled job, a headless model run or a template engine. Every quote is a literal match to the published piece.
Where realistic synthetic media is present, apply the native AI label where the destination supports it; never add illustration boilerplate to public copy.
On YouTube a meme is a real video file, never a still posing as video.

Share mechanic: recognition of one specific situation the receiver is in, so the sender's message is that this is them; the share block names that situation as its moment. It stays a proposal in the brief until content-engine adopts it as a production standard through its own route.
Before Krish sees it: a complete share block (social/share.json), no generic share call to action in the copy, and a blind send test whose reader names the declared receiver and job (crew/send-test).
Bind publication approval to the exact account, caption, ordered asset hashes, metadata and proposed time.
After a save, wait and independently reopen; reconcile uncertain outcomes before retrying.
measurements: Primary measure (Krish, 28 October 2026): sends, meaning native shares, per reach and saves per reach against the format's own channel median; a house hypothesis until MYMU's own dated data confirms it (lesson share-rate-measure).
Dated exposed reach and meaningful engagement, preserving missing values.
Relevant follower/profile movement and source-attributed publication subscriptions where exposed.
24-hour, 72-hour and seven-day readback after actual publication; no financial ROI inference from draft counts.
